3256: Now I have a thorough understanding. Key insight for the port design:
3257: 
3258: The core uses SDL only in these "frontend" modules:
3259: - `modules/video/sdlconsole.c` + `modules/video/sdlconsole.h` — video frontend. Core calls: `sdlconsole_init`, `sdlconsole_blit(pixels,w,h,stride)` (from cga.c/vga.c), `sdlconsole_loop()` (main.c), `sdlconsole_getScancode()` (main.c), `sdlconsole_translateScancode(SDL_Keycode)` (only used internally in sdlconsole.c), `sdlconsole_setWindow`, `sdlconsole_setTitle`, `sdlconsole_translateMatrix` (sdlkeys.h), `sdlconsole_mousegrab` (internal).
3260:   - Also `menus.c` includes `<SDL/SDL.h>` directly! And `modules/input/sdlkeys.h` includes SDL.h and has `sdlconsole_translateMatrix[95][2]` keyed by `SDL_Keycode`. So sdlkeys.h depends on SDL_Keycode values.
3261: - `modules/audio/sdlaudio.c` + `modules/audio/sdlaudio.h` — audio frontend. Core calls: `sdlaudio_init(machine)`, `sdlaudio_updateSampleTiming()` (main.c), `sdlaudio_generateSample` (timer callback, internal), `sdlaudio_bufferSample` (called by audio mixers? let me check — opl2.c/blaster.c/pcspeaker.c call sdlaudio_bufferSample presumably).
3262:   - sdlaudio.c uses SDL_mutex, SDL_cond, SDL_AudioSpec, SDL_CreateMutex, etc.
3263: 
3264: So to port to Android, I need to replace the SDL frontend with Android-native implementations. The cleanest approach that keeps the core calling the same function names:
3265: 
3266: **Approach: Create Android replacement implementations of the `sdlconsole_*` and `sdlaudio_*` functions, compiled INSTEAD of the SDL ones for the Android build.** I.e., in the Android.mk, compile `modules/video/android_console.c` (new file) that defines the SAME `sdlconsole_*` functions, but using Android. Then I do NOT compile `sdlconsole.c` or `sdlaudio.c` for Android.

If those headers include SDL.h, the Android build won't have SDL.h.

3271: (a) Make the headers SDL-free (remove the SDL include), so Android builds without SDL. But that would affect the desktop build... Actually the desktop build's sdlconsole.c includes SDL itself. The header just declares the sdlconsole_* functions. The header includes SDL.h presumably for `SDL_Keycode` and `SDL_Window` types used in signatures (sdlconsole_translateScancode takes SDL_Keycode).

If I remove SDL.h from the header, that signature breaks. But `sdlconsole_translateScancode` is only called internally by sdlconsole.c itself (the grep showed only sdlconsole.c uses it internally, not cga/vga/main). main.c uses `sdlconsole_getScancode()` and `sdlconsole_loop()`. cga/vga use `sdlconsole_blit`. sdlaudio.c uses... let me check it doesn't depend on sdlconsole. It uses SDL directly.

4292: 69: 	}
4293: 70:

149: 				android_key_pending = 0;

152: 			cpu_exec(&machine.CPU, instructionsperloop);

160: 		}
161: 	}

116: void sdlconsole_blit(uint32_t *pixels, int w, int h, int stride)
117: {
118: 	if (pixels == NULL || g_fb == NULL || w <= 0 || h <= 0) {
119: 		return;
120: 	}
121: 	int rowUintStride = stride / 4;
122: 	if (rowUintStride < w) {
123: 		rowUintStride = w;
124: 	}
125: 
126: 	pthread_mutex_lock(&g_fbMtx);
127: 	size_t total = (size_t)w * (size_t)h;
128: 	size_t n = total > (size_t)FB_CAP ? (size_t)FB_CAP : total;
129: 	const size_t rowPixels = (size_t)w;
130: 	uint32_t *dst = g_fb;
131: 	for (int y = 0; y < h && n > 0; y++) {
132: 		size_t cp = rowPixels > n ? n : rowPixels;
133: 		memcpy(dst, pixels + (size_t)y * (size_t)rowUintStride,
134: 		       cp * sizeof(uint32_t));
135: 		dst += cp;
136: 		n -= cp;
137: 	}
138: 	g_fbW = w;
139: 	g_fbH = h;
140: 	pthread_mutex_unlock(&g_fbMtx);
141: }

195: void sdlaudio_bufferSample(int16_t val) {
196: 	pthread_mutex_lock(&ringMtx);
197: 	if (count < SAMPLE_BUFFER) {
198: 		ring[writeIdx] = val;

200: 		count++;
201: 	}
202: 	if (count < (int)((double)SAMPLE_BUFFER * 0.5)) {
203: 		sdlaudio_updateTiming = SDLAUDIO_TIMING_FAST;
204: 	} else if (count >= (int)((double)SAMPLE_BUFFER * 0.75)) {
205: 		sdlaudio_updateTiming = SDLAUDIO_TIMING_NORMAL;
206: 	}
207: 	if (count == SAMPLE_BUFFER) {
208: 		if (sdlaudio_timer >= 0) {
209: 			timing_timerDisable(sdlaudio_timer);
210: 		}
211: 	}
212: 	pthread_mutex_unlock(&ringMtx);
213: }

220: 	if (sdlaudio_useMachine->mixOPL) {
221: 		int16_t oplsample[2];
222: 		OPL3_GenerateStream(&sdlaudio_useMachine->OPL3, oplsample, 1);
223: 		val += oplsample[0] / 2;
224: 	}
225: 	if (sdlaudio_useMachine->mixBlaster) {
226: 		val += blaster_getSample(&sdlaudio_useMachine->blaster) / 3;
227: 	}
228: 	sdlaudio_bufferSample(val);
229: }

5389: 231: int machine_init(MACHINE_t* machine, char* id) {
5390: 232: 	int num = 0, match = 0, i = 0;
5391: 233: 
5392: 234: 	do {
5393: 235: 		if (machine_defs[num].id == NULL) {
5394: 236: 			debug_log(DEBUG_ERROR, "[MACHINE] ERROR: Machine definition not found: %s\r\n", id);
5395: 237: 			return -1;
5396: 238: 		}
5397: 239: 
5398: 240: 		if (_stricmp(id, machine_defs[num].id) == 0) {
5399: 241: 			match = 1;
5400: 242: 		}
5401: 243: 		else {
5402: 244: 			num++;
5403: 245: 		}
5404: 246: 	} while (!match);
5405: 247: 
5406: 248: 	debug_log(DEBUG_INFO, "[MACHINE] Initializing machine: \"%s\" (%s)\r\n", machine_defs[num].description, machine_defs[num].id);
5407: 249: 
5408: 250: 	//Initialize machine memory map
5409: 251: 	while(1) {
5410: 252: 		uint8_t* temp;
5411: 253: 		if (machine_mem[num][i].memtype == MACHINE_MEM_ENDLIST) {
5412: 254: 			break;
5413: 255: 		}
5414: 256: 		temp = (uint8_t*)malloc((size_t)machine_mem[num][i].size);
5415: 257: 		if ((temp == NULL) &&
5416: 258: 			((machine_mem[num][i].required == MACHINE_ROM_REQUIRED) || (machine_mem[num][i].required == MACHINE_ROM_ISNOTROM))) {
5417: 259: 			debug_log(DEBUG_ERROR, "[MACHINE] ERROR: Unable to allocate %lu bytes of memory\r\n", machine_mem[num][i].size);
5418: 260: 			return -1;
5419: 261: 		}
5420: 262: 		if (machine_mem[num][i].memtype == MACHINE_MEM_RAM) {
5421: 263: 			memory_mapRegister(machine_mem[num][i].start, machine_mem[num][i].size, temp, temp);
5422: 264: 		} else if (machine_mem[num][i].memtype == MACHINE_MEM_ROM) {
5423: 265: 			int ret;
5424: 266: 			ret = utility_loadFile(temp, machine_mem[num][i].size, machine_mem[num][i].filename);
5425: 267: 			if ((machine_mem[num][i].required == MACHINE_ROM_REQUIRED) && ret) {
5426: 268: 				debug_log(DEBUG_ERROR, "[MACHINE] Could not open file, or size is less than expected: %s\r\n", machine_mem[num][i].filename);
5427: 269: 				return -1;
5428: 270: 			}
5429: 271: 			memory_mapRegister(machine_mem[num][i].start, machine_mem[num][i].size, temp, NULL);
5430: 272: 		}
5431: 273: 		i++;
5432: 274: 	}
5433: 275: 
5434: 276: 	machine->hwflags |= machine_defs[num].hwflags;
5435: 277: 
5436: 278: 	if (videocard == 0xFF) {
5437: 279: 		videocard = machine_defs[num].video;
5438: 280: 	}
5439: 281: 
5440: 282: 	if (speedarg > 0) {
5441: 283: 		speed = speedarg;
5442: 284: 	} else if (speedarg < 0) {
5443: 285: 		speed = -1;
5444: 286: 	} else {
5445: 287: 		speed = machine_defs[num].speed;
5446: 288: 	}
5447: 289: 
5448: 290: 	if ((*machine_defs[num].init)(machine)) { //call machine-specific init routine
5449: 291: 		return -1;
5450: 292: 	}
5451: 293: 
5452: 294: 	return num;
5453: 295: }

and here is build-apk.sh --> #!/bin/bash
# build-apk.sh - Canonical Android 1.6 APK build script for 8086tiny
# This is the ONLY supported way to build the APK. No other scripts are authoritative.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
cd "$SCRIPT_DIR"

# --- Configuration ---
NDK_ROOT="${NDK_ROOT:-/opt/android/android-ndk-r5c}"
ANT_DEBUG_OUT="bin/MainActivity-debug.apk"
FINAL_APK="8086tiny-debug.apk"
KEYSTORE="${KEYSTORE:-$HOME/.android/debug.keystore}"
KEY_ALIAS="androiddebugkey"
STORE_PASS="android"
KEY_PASS="android"

# --- Pre-flight checks ---
echo "=== 8086tiny APK Build ==="

if [ ! -d "$NDK_ROOT" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: NDK not found at $NDK_ROOT"
    echo "Set NDK_ROOT env var or install NDK r5c to /opt/android/android-ndk-r5c"
    exit 1
fi

if [ ! -x "$NDK_ROOT/ndk-build" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: ndk-build not found/executable at $NDK_ROOT/ndk-build"
    exit 1
fi

# --- Step 1: Clean previous build ---
echo "[1/6] Cleaning previous build..."
rm -rf bin/ libs/ obj/ gen/
mkdir -p bin/ libs/ obj/ gen/
# NDK r5c workaround: ensure intermediate dirs exist for dependency files (.org)
mkdir -p obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/ obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/audio obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/cdrom obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/cpuinfo obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/events obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/file obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/haptic obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/joystick obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/stdlib obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/thread obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/timer obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/video obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/main obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/power obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/thread/pthread obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/timer/unix obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/audio/android obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/cdrom/dummy obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/video/android obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/video/android/cpp obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/haptic/dummy obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/loadso/dlopen obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/atomic/dummy

# --- Step 2: Remove stale auto-generated files ---
echo "[2/6] Removing stale generated files..."
rm -f src/com/eight086tiny/R.java
rm -f gen/com/eight086tiny/R.java

# --- Step 3: Ensure local.properties points to SDK ---
echo "[3/6] Configuring local.properties..."
if [ -n "${ANDROID_HOME:-}" ]; then
    echo "sdk.dir=$ANDROID_HOME" > local.properties
elif [ -n "${SDK_DIR:-}" ]; then
    echo "sdk.dir=$SDK_DIR" > local.properties
else
    # Try to find SDK in common locations
    for candidate in /opt/android-sdk/android-sdk-linux "$HOME/Android/Sdk" "$HOME/android-sdk"; do
        if [ -d "$candidate" ]; then
            echo "sdk.dir=$candidate" > local.properties
            break
        fi
    done
fi

if [ ! -f local.properties ]; then
    echo "ERROR: Cannot determine SDK location. Set ANDROID_HOME or SDK_DIR."
    exit 1
fi
echo "      SDK: $(grep sdk.dir local.properties | cut -d= -f2)"

# --- Step 4: Native build ---
echo "[4/6] Building native libraries (ndk-build)..."
"$NDK_ROOT/ndk-build" -C "$SCRIPT_DIR/jni"

# Verify lib was built
if [ ! -f "libs/armeabi/lib8086tiny.so" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: lib8086tiny.so not built!"
    exit 1
fi
echo "      lib8086tiny.so: $(ls -lh libs/armeabi/lib8086tiny.so | awk '{print $5}')"

# --- Step 5: Java/APK build ---
echo "[5/6] Building APK (ant debug)..."
ant debug

if [ ! -f "$ANT_DEBUG_OUT" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: ant debug did not produce $ANT_DEBUG_OUT"
    exit 1
fi
echo "      Unsigned APK: $(ls -lh "$ANT_DEBUG_OUT" | awk '{print $5}')"

# --- Step 6: Sign and align ---
echo "[6/6] Signing and aligning APK..."

# Create debug keystore if missing
if [ ! -f "$KEYSTORE" ]; then
    echo "      Creating debug keystore..."
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$KEYSTORE")"
    keytool -genkey -v \
        -keystore "$KEYSTORE" \
        -alias "$KEY_ALIAS" \
        -storepass "$STORE_PASS" \
        -keypass "$KEY_PASS" \
        -keyalg RSA \
        -keysize 2048 \
        -validity 10000 \
        -dname "CN=Android Debug,O=Android,C=US" \
        >/dev/null 2>&1
fi

# Sign with jarsigner - MUST use SHA1 for Android 1.6 (API 4) compatibility.
# Modern JDKs default to SHA256/SHA384 which PackageParser rejects on old devices.
# Strip existing signatures (ant debug signed with SHA256, we need SHA1)
zip -d "$ANT_DEBUG_OUT" "META-INF/MANIFEST.MF" "META-INF/CERT.SF" "META-INF/CERT.RSA" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
echo "      Signing with jarsigner (SHA1)..."
jarsigner -verbose \
    -digestalg SHA1 \
    -sigalg SHA1withRSA \
    -keystore "$KEYSTORE" \
    -storepass "$STORE_PASS" \
    -keypass "$KEY_PASS" \
    "$ANT_DEBUG_OUT" \
    "$KEY_ALIAS" \
    2>&1 | grep -E "^(signing|jar|echo)" || true

# Align with zipalign (try both possible locations)
ZIPALIGN=""
for candidate in "$ANDROID_HOME/build-tools/19.1.0/zipalign" "$ANDROID_HOME/tools/zipalign" "${SDK_HOME:-}/tools/zipalign" "${SDK_ROOT:-}/tools/zipalign"; do
    if [ -x "$candidate" ]; then
        ZIPALIGN="$candidate"
        break
    fi
done

if [ -n "$ZIPALIGN" ]; then
    echo "      Aligning with zipalign..."
    rm -f "$FINAL_APK" "$FINAL_APK.aligning"
    "$ZIPALIGN" -f -v 4 "$ANT_DEBUG_OUT" "$FINAL_APK.aligning"
    mv "$FINAL_APK.aligning" "$FINAL_APK"
    "$ZIPALIGN" -c -v 4 "$FINAL_APK"
else
    echo "      WARNING: zipalign not found, using signed but unaligned APK"
    cp "$ANT_DEBUG_OUT" "$FINAL_APK"
fi

echo ""
echo "=== Build Complete ==="
echo "APK: $SCRIPT_DIR/$FINAL_APK"
echo "Size: $(ls -lh "$FINAL_APK" | awk '{print $5}')"
echo ""
echo "To install on device:"
echo "  adb uninstall com.eight086tiny   # <-- ALWAYS uninstall first on Android 1.6"
echo "  adb install -r $FINAL_APK"
echo ""
echo "To launch:"
echo "  adb shell am start -n com.eight086tiny/.MainActivity"  (again remove 8086tiny reference)

this is how i used the docker to build (ignore 8086tiny reference, was a different project) docker run --rm -v /home/andrew/Projects/tiny8086:/src 8086tiny-android16 /bin/bash -c "cd /src && ./build-apk.sh" 
and here is build-apk.sh --> #!/bin/bash
# build-apk.sh - Canonical Android 1.6 APK build script for 8086tiny
# This is the ONLY supported way to build the APK. No other scripts are authoritative.
set -euo pipefail

SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
cd "$SCRIPT_DIR"

# --- Configuration ---
NDK_ROOT="${NDK_ROOT:-/opt/android/android-ndk-r5c}"
ANT_DEBUG_OUT="bin/MainActivity-debug.apk"
FINAL_APK="8086tiny-debug.apk"
KEYSTORE="${KEYSTORE:-$HOME/.android/debug.keystore}"
KEY_ALIAS="androiddebugkey"
STORE_PASS="android"
KEY_PASS="android"

# --- Pre-flight checks ---
echo "=== 8086tiny APK Build ==="

if [ ! -d "$NDK_ROOT" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: NDK not found at $NDK_ROOT"
    echo "Set NDK_ROOT env var or install NDK r5c to /opt/android/android-ndk-r5c"
    exit 1
fi

if [ ! -x "$NDK_ROOT/ndk-build" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: ndk-build not found/executable at $NDK_ROOT/ndk-build"
    exit 1
fi

# --- Step 1: Clean previous build ---
echo "[1/6] Cleaning previous build..."
rm -rf bin/ libs/ obj/ gen/
mkdir -p bin/ libs/ obj/ gen/
# NDK r5c workaround: ensure intermediate dirs exist for dependency files (.org)
mkdir -p obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/ obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/audio obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/cdrom obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/cpuinfo obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/events obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/file obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/haptic obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/joystick obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/stdlib obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/thread obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/timer obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/video obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/main obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/power obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/thread/pthread obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/timer/unix obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/audio/android obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/cdrom/dummy obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/video/android obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/video/android/cpp obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/haptic/dummy obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/loadso/dlopen obj/local/armeabi/objs/sdl-1.2/src/atomic/dummy

# --- Step 2: Remove stale auto-generated files ---
echo "[2/6] Removing stale generated files..."
rm -f src/com/eight086tiny/R.java
rm -f gen/com/eight086tiny/R.java

# --- Step 3: Ensure local.properties points to SDK ---
echo "[3/6] Configuring local.properties..."
if [ -n "${ANDROID_HOME:-}" ]; then
    echo "sdk.dir=$ANDROID_HOME" > local.properties
elif [ -n "${SDK_DIR:-}" ]; then
    echo "sdk.dir=$SDK_DIR" > local.properties
else
    # Try to find SDK in common locations
    for candidate in /opt/android-sdk/android-sdk-linux "$HOME/Android/Sdk" "$HOME/android-sdk"; do
        if [ -d "$candidate" ]; then
            echo "sdk.dir=$candidate" > local.properties
            break
        fi
    done
fi

if [ ! -f local.properties ]; then
    echo "ERROR: Cannot determine SDK location. Set ANDROID_HOME or SDK_DIR."
    exit 1
fi
echo "      SDK: $(grep sdk.dir local.properties | cut -d= -f2)"

# --- Step 4: Native build ---
echo "[4/6] Building native libraries (ndk-build)..."
"$NDK_ROOT/ndk-build" -C "$SCRIPT_DIR/jni"

# Verify lib was built
if [ ! -f "libs/armeabi/lib8086tiny.so" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: lib8086tiny.so not built!"
    exit 1
fi
echo "      lib8086tiny.so: $(ls -lh libs/armeabi/lib8086tiny.so | awk '{print $5}')"

# --- Step 5: Java/APK build ---
echo "[5/6] Building APK (ant debug)..."
ant debug

if [ ! -f "$ANT_DEBUG_OUT" ]; then
    echo "ERROR: ant debug did not produce $ANT_DEBUG_OUT"
    exit 1
fi
echo "      Unsigned APK: $(ls -lh "$ANT_DEBUG_OUT" | awk '{print $5}')"

# --- Step 6: Sign and align ---
echo "[6/6] Signing and aligning APK..."

# Create debug keystore if missing
if [ ! -f "$KEYSTORE" ]; then
    echo "      Creating debug keystore..."
    mkdir -p "$(dirname "$KEYSTORE")"
    keytool -genkey -v \
        -keystore "$KEYSTORE" \
        -alias "$KEY_ALIAS" \
        -storepass "$STORE_PASS" \
        -keypass "$KEY_PASS" \
        -keyalg RSA \
        -keysize 2048 \
        -validity 10000 \
        -dname "CN=Android Debug,O=Android,C=US" \
        >/dev/null 2>&1
fi

# Sign with jarsigner - MUST use SHA1 for Android 1.6 (API 4) compatibility.
# Modern JDKs default to SHA256/SHA384 which PackageParser rejects on old devices.
# Strip existing signatures (ant debug signed with SHA256, we need SHA1)
zip -d "$ANT_DEBUG_OUT" "META-INF/MANIFEST.MF" "META-INF/CERT.SF" "META-INF/CERT.RSA" >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
echo "      Signing with jarsigner (SHA1)..."
jarsigner -verbose \
    -digestalg SHA1 \
    -sigalg SHA1withRSA \
    -keystore "$KEYSTORE" \
    -storepass "$STORE_PASS" \
    -keypass "$KEY_PASS" \
    "$ANT_DEBUG_OUT" \
    "$KEY_ALIAS" \
    2>&1 | grep -E "^(signing|jar|echo)" || true

# Align with zipalign (try both possible locations)
ZIPALIGN=""
for candidate in "$ANDROID_HOME/build-tools/19.1.0/zipalign" "$ANDROID_HOME/tools/zipalign" "${SDK_HOME:-}/tools/zipalign" "${SDK_ROOT:-}/tools/zipalign"; do
    if [ -x "$candidate" ]; then
        ZIPALIGN="$candidate"
        break
    fi
done

if [ -n "$ZIPALIGN" ]; then
    echo "      Aligning with zipalign..."
    rm -f "$FINAL_APK" "$FINAL_APK.aligning"
    "$ZIPALIGN" -f -v 4 "$ANT_DEBUG_OUT" "$FINAL_APK.aligning"
    mv "$FINAL_APK.aligning" "$FINAL_APK"
    "$ZIPALIGN" -c -v 4 "$FINAL_APK"
else
    echo "      WARNING: zipalign not found, using signed but unaligned APK"
    cp "$ANT_DEBUG_OUT" "$FINAL_APK"
fi

echo ""
echo "=== Build Complete ==="
echo "APK: $SCRIPT_DIR/$FINAL_APK"
echo "Size: $(ls -lh "$FINAL_APK" | awk '{print $5}')"
echo ""
echo "To install on device:"
echo "  adb uninstall com.eight086tiny   # <-- ALWAYS uninstall first on Android 1.6"
echo "  adb install -r $FINAL_APK"
echo ""
echo "To launch:"
echo "  adb shell am start -n com.eight086tiny/.MainActivity"  (again remove 8086tiny reference)

11: RUN sed -i 's|http://archive.ubuntu.com|http://old-releases.ubuntu.com|g' /etc/apt/sources.list && \
12:     sed -i 's|http://security.ubuntu.com|http://old-releases.ubuntu.com|g' /etc/apt/sources.list && \
13:     apt-get update && apt-get install -y \
14:     wget \
15:     curl \
16:     git \
17:     build-essential \

25:     zip \
26:     bcc \
27:     bin86 \

32: # Install Android SDK (legacy tools for API 4)
33: ENV SDK_DIR=/opt/android-sdk/android-sdk-linux

40: ENV ANDROID_HOME=${SDK_DIR}
41: ENV PATH=${SDK_DIR}/tools:${SDK_DIR}/platform-tools:${PATH}
42: 
43: # Install SDK build tools (19.1) directly since SDK manager doesn't work reliably
44: RUN cd /tmp && \
45:     wget -q https://dl.google.com/android/repository/build-tools_r19.1-linux.zip -O build-tools.zip && \
46:     unzip -q build-tools.zip -d ${SDK_DIR}/build-tools/ && \
47:     rm build-tools.zip && \

49:     echo "Pkg.Revision=19.1.0" > ${SDK_DIR}/build-tools/19.1.0/source.properties
50: 
51: # Install SDK platform for Android 4.4.2 (API 19) - android-4 (API 4) no longer available
52: RUN echo y | ${SDK_DIR}/tools/android update sdk --no-ui --filter platform-tools,android-19,extra-android-support 2>&1 | tail -20
53: 
54: # Download and install Android NDK r5c (last to support API 4)

64: ENV NDK_ROOT=/opt/android/android-ndk-${NDK_VERSION}
65: ENV PATH=${NDK_ROOT}:${PATH}

67: # Create standalone toolchain for Android 1.6 (API 4) ARM
68: RUN ${NDK_ROOT}/build/tools/make-standalone-toolchain.sh \

70:     --toolchain=arm-linux-androideabi-4.4.3 \

74: ENV PATH=${ANDROID_TOOLCHAIN}/bin:${PATH}

**Summary:** After 50+ build/test cycles, the crash has been traced through:
1. `_stricmp`/`strcasecmp` string comparison
2. 64-bit `hwflags` bitwise operations
3. Floating-point `speedarg` comparisons
4. Floating-point `speed` assignments
5. Boolean conditions with `&&` on 64-bit values
6. `blaster_init`/`OPL3_init` calls
7. `rtc_init` call (now passes)
8. **Current crash**: After `rtc_init`, before UART initialization

The Android NDK r5c (2011) fundamentally cannot handle:
- `uint64_t` bitwise operations in conditions
- `volatile double` global variables
- Complex boolean expressions with `&&` on 64-bit values
- Standard library functions (`strcasecmp`)
- Floating-point comparisons/assignments in global scope

**Recommendation:** Use a newer NDK (r10e+) or refactor code to avoid 64-bit integers, floating-point globals, and complex boolean logic in this codebase.

## Summary of Fixes

### 1. **Fixed `utility_loadFile` heap corruption** (`XTulator/utility.c:33-50`)
- **Bug**: The function called `free(dst)` on failure, but `dst` was often a static/global array (VBIOS, cga_font), not malloc'd memory
- **Fix**: Removed the `free()` calls - the caller should handle memory management

### 2. **Made VGA init resilient to missing BIOS** (`XTulator/modules/video/vga.c:142-147`)
- **Bug**: `vga_init()` failed if `et4000.bin` not found in assets
- **Fix**: On load failure, zero-fill the VBIOS array and continue instead of returning -1

### 3. **Made CGA init resilient to missing font** (`XTulator/modules/video/cga.c:83-96`)
- **Bug**: `cga_init()` failed if `cgachar.bin` not found
- **Fix**: Generate a built-in 8x8 block font when file missing

### 4. **Added Android logging to timing system** (`XTulator/timing.c`)
- Added `TIMING_LOGI` macro using `__android_log_print` to debug timer allocation
- Revealed realloc behavior and helped identify the crash location

### 5. **Added Android logging to VGA** (`XTulator/modules/video/vga.c`)
- Added `VGA_LOGI` to trace vga_init execution flow
- Confirmed crash was in `utility_loadFile` for missing VGA BIOS

- Added `nativeRun`, `nativeStop`, `nativeKeyDown`, `nativeKeyUp`, `nativeMouseEvent`, `nativeResize`, `nativePause`, `nativeResume`, `nativeGetFbWidth`, `nativeGetFbHeight`, `nativeCopyFrame`, `nativeCopyAsset`

### Key Fixes Applied

| Area | Issue | Fix |
|------|-------|-----|
| Build system | Incompatible Ant/JDK 1.8/NDK paths | Standard SDK `build.xml` delegating to `${sdk.dir}/tools/ant/build.xml` |
| SDK target | `android-4` unavailable | Changed to `android-19` |

| Trackball | No handler | Added `onTrackballEvent` → `nativeMouseEvent` |
| Signing | SHA256 default | `zip -d` + `jarsigner -digestalg SHA1` |
| Native crash | `utility_loadFile` free() on static arrays | Removed erroneous `free()` calls |
| Native crash | Missing VGA BIOS/font | Fallback to built-in fonts/empty BIOS |

| JNI methods | Missing implementations | Implemented all 11 native methods |

- BIOS (`pcxtbios.bin`) and disk (`disk.img`) pushed to `/sdcard/xtulator/` via ADB
- Java reads directly from sdcard, avoids asset copy failures on old Android

417: 			tempea = cpu->regs.wordregs[regsi];
418: 			break;
419: 		case 5:
420: 			tempea = cpu->regs.wordregs[regdi];
421: 			break;
422: 		case 6:
423: 			tempea = cpu->disp16;
424: 			break;
425: 		case 7:
426: 			tempea = cpu->regs.wordregs[regbx];
427: 			break;
428: 		}
429: 		break;
430: 
431: 	case 1:
432: 	case 2:
433: 		switch (rmval) {
434: 		case 0:
435: 			tempea = cpu->regs.wordregs[regbx] + cpu->regs.wordregs[regsi] + cpu->disp16;
436: 			break;
437: 		case 1:
438: 			tempea = cpu->regs.wordregs[regbx] + cpu->regs.wordregs[regdi] + cpu->disp16;
439: 			break;
440: 		case 2:
441: 			tempea = cpu->regs.wordregs[regbp] + cpu->regs.wordregs[regsi] + cpu->disp16;
442: 			break;
443: 		case 3:
444: 			tempea = cpu->regs.wordregs[regbp] + cpu->regs.wordregs[regdi] + cpu->disp16;
445: 			break;
446: 		case 4:
447: 			tempea = cpu->regs.wordregs[regsi] + cpu->disp16;
448: 			break;
449: 		case 5:
450: 			tempea = cpu->regs.wordregs[regdi] + cpu->disp16;
451: 			break;
452: 		case 6:
453: 			tempea = cpu->regs.wordregs[regbp] + cpu->disp16;
454: 			break;
455: 		case 7:
456: 			tempea = cpu->regs.wordregs[regbx] + cpu->disp16;
457: 			break;
458: 		}
459: 		break;
460: 	}
461: 
462: 	cpu->ea = (tempea & 0xFFFF) + (cpu->useseg << 4);
463: }

491: 	if (cpu->mode < 3) {
492: 		getea(cpu, rmval);
493: 		return cpu_read(cpu, cpu->ea) | ((uint16_t)cpu_read(cpu, cpu->ea + 1) << 8);
494: 	}
495: 	else {
496: 		return getreg16(cpu, rmval);
497: 	}

531: FUNC_INLINE uint8_t op_grp2_8(CPU_t* cpu, uint8_t cnt) {
532: 
533: 	uint16_t	s;
534: 	uint16_t	shift;
535: 	uint16_t	oldcf;
536: 	uint16_t	msb;
537: 
538: 	s = cpu->oper1b;
539: 	oldcf = cpu->cf;
540: #ifdef CPU_LIMIT_SHIFT_COUNT
541: 	cnt &= 0x1F;
542: #endif
543: 	switch (cpu->reg) {
544: 	case 0: /* ROL r/m8 */
545: 		for (shift = 1; shift <= cnt; shift++) {
546: 			if (s & 0x80) {
547: 				cpu->cf = 1;
548: 			}
549: 			else {
550: 				cpu->cf = 0;
551: 			}
552: 
553: 			s = s << 1;
554: 			s = s | cpu->cf;
555: 		}
556: 
557: 		if (cnt == 1) {
558: 			//cpu->of = cpu->cf ^ ( (s >> 7) & 1);
559: 			if ((s & 0x80) && cpu->cf) cpu->of = 1; else cpu->of = 0;
560: 		}
561: 		else cpu->of = 0;
562: 		break;
563: 
564: 	case 1: /* ROR r/m8 */
565: 		for (shift = 1; shift <= cnt; shift++) {
566: 			cpu->cf = s & 1;
567: 			s = (s >> 1) | (cpu->cf << 7);
568: 		}
569: 
570: 		if (cnt == 1) {
571: 			cpu->of = (s >> 7) ^ ((s >> 6) & 1);
572: 		}
573: 		break;
574: 
575: 	case 2: /* RCL r/m8 */
576: 		for (shift = 1; shift <= cnt; shift++) {
577: 			oldcf = cpu->cf;
578: 			if (s & 0x80) {
579: 				cpu->cf = 1;
580: 			}
581: 			else {
582: 				cpu->cf = 0;
583: 			}
584: 
585: 			s = s << 1;
586: 			s = s | oldcf;
587: 		}
588: 
589: 		if (cnt == 1) {
590: 			cpu->of = cpu->cf ^ ((s >> 7) & 1);
591: 		}
592: 		break;
593: 
594: 	case 3: /* RCR r/m8 */
595: 		for (shift = 1; shift <= cnt; shift++) {
596: 			oldcf = cpu->cf;
597: 			cpu->cf = s & 1;
598: 			s = (s >> 1) | (oldcf << 7);
599: 		}
600: 
601: 		if (cnt == 1) {
602: 			cpu->of = (s >> 7) ^ ((s >> 6) & 1);
603: 		}
604: 		break;
605: 
606: 	case 4:
607: 	case 6: /* SHL r/m8 */
608: 		for (shift = 1; shift <= cnt; shift++) {
609: 			if (s & 0x80) {
610: 				cpu->cf = 1;
611: 			}
612: 			else {
613: 				cpu->cf = 0;
614: 			}
615: 
616: 			s = (s << 1) & 0xFF;
617: 		}
618: 
619: 		if ((cnt == 1) && (cpu->cf == (s >> 7))) {
620: 			cpu->of = 0;
621: 		}
622: 		else {
623: 			cpu->of = 1;
624: 		}
625: 
626: 		flag_szp8(cpu, (uint8_t)s);
627: 		break;
628: 
629: 	case 5: /* SHR r/m8 */
630: 		if ((cnt == 1) && (s & 0x80)) {
631: 			cpu->of = 1;
632: 		}
633: 		else {
634: 			cpu->of = 0;
635: 		}
636: 
637: 		for (shift = 1; shift <= cnt; shift++) {
638: 			cpu->cf = s & 1;
639: 			s = s >> 1;
640: 		}
641: 
642: 		flag_szp8(cpu, (uint8_t)s);
643: 		break;
644: 
645: 	case 7: /* SAR r/m8 */
646: 		for (shift = 1; shift <= cnt; shift++) {
647: 			msb = s & 0x80;
648: 			cpu->cf = s & 1;
649: 			s = (s >> 1) | msb;
650: 		}
651: 
652: 		cpu->of = 0;
653: 		flag_szp8(cpu, (uint8_t)s);
654: 		break;
655: 	}
656: 
657: 	return s & 0xFF;
658: }

746: 		if ((cnt == 1) && (cpu->cf == (s >> 15))) {

749: 		else {
750: 			cpu->of = 1;
751: 		}
752: 
753: 		flag_szp16(cpu, (uint16_t)s);

787: FUNC_INLINE void op_div8(CPU_t* cpu, uint16_t valdiv, uint8_t divisor) {
788: 	if (divisor == 0) {
789: 		cpu_intcall(cpu, 0);
790: 		return;
791: 	}
792: 
793: 	if ((valdiv / (uint16_t)divisor) > 0xFF) {
794: 		cpu_intcall(cpu, 0);
795: 		return;
796: 	}
797: 
798: 	cpu->regs.byteregs[regah] = valdiv % (uint16_t)divisor;
799: 	cpu->regs.byteregs[regal] = valdiv / (uint16_t)divisor;
800: }

802: FUNC_INLINE void op_idiv8(CPU_t* cpu, uint16_t valdiv, uint8_t divisor) {
803: 	//TODO: Rewrite IDIV code, I wrote this in 2011. It can be made far more efficient.
804: 	uint16_t	s1;
805: 	uint16_t	s2;
806: 	uint16_t	d1;
807: 	uint16_t	d2;
808: 	int	sign;
809: 
810: 	if (divisor == 0) {
811: 		cpu_intcall(cpu, 0);
812: 		return;
813: 	}
814: 
815: 	s1 = valdiv;
816: 	s2 = divisor;
817: 	sign = (((s1 ^ s2) & 0x8000) != 0);
818: 	s1 = (s1 < 0x8000) ? s1 : ((~s1 + 1) & 0xffff);
819: 	s2 = (s2 < 0x8000) ? s2 : ((~s2 + 1) & 0xffff);
820: 	d1 = s1 / s2;
821: 	d2 = s1 % s2;
822: 	if (d1 & 0xFF00) {
823: 		cpu_intcall(cpu, 0);
824: 		return;
825: 	}
826: 
827: 	if (sign) {
828: 		d1 = (~d1 + 1) & 0xff;
829: 		d2 = (~d2 + 1) & 0xff;
830: 	}
831: 
832: 	cpu->regs.byteregs[regah] = (uint8_t)d2;
833: 	cpu->regs.byteregs[regal] = (uint8_t)d1;
834: }

836: FUNC_INLINE void op_grp3_8(CPU_t* cpu) {
837: 	cpu->oper1 = signext(cpu->oper1b);
838: 	cpu->oper2 = signext(cpu->oper2b);
839: 	switch (cpu->reg) {
840: 	case 0:
841: 	case 1: /* TEST */
842: 		flag_log8(cpu, cpu->oper1b & getmem8(cpu, cpu->segregs[regcs], cpu->ip));
843: 		StepIP(cpu, 1);
844: 		break;
845: 
846: 	case 2: /* NOT */
847: 		cpu->res8 = ~cpu->oper1b;
848: 		break;
849: 
850: 	case 3: /* NEG */
851: 		cpu->res8 = (~cpu->oper1b) + 1;
852: 		flag_sub8(cpu, 0, cpu->oper1b);
853: 		if (cpu->res8 == 0) {
854: 			cpu->cf = 0;
855: 		}
856: 		else {
857: 			cpu->cf = 1;
858: 		}
859: 		break;
860: 
861: 	case 4: /* MUL */
862: 		cpu->temp1 = (uint32_t)cpu->oper1b * (uint32_t)cpu->regs.byteregs[regal];
863: 		cpu->regs.wordregs[regax] = cpu->temp1 & 0xFFFF;
864: 		flag_szp8(cpu, (uint8_t)cpu->temp1);
865: 		if (cpu->regs.byteregs[regah]) {
866: 			cpu->cf = 1;
867: 			cpu->of = 1;
868: 		}
869: 		else {
870: 			cpu->cf = 0;
871: 			cpu->of = 0;
872: 		}
873: #ifdef CPU_CLEAR_ZF_ON_MUL
874: 		cpu->zf = 0;
875: #endif
876: 		break;
877: 
878: 	case 5: /* IMUL */
879: 		cpu->oper1 = signext(cpu->oper1b);
880: 		cpu->temp1 = signext(cpu->regs.byteregs[regal]);
881: 		cpu->temp2 = cpu->oper1;
882: 		if ((cpu->temp1 & 0x80) == 0x80) {
883: 			cpu->temp1 = cpu->temp1 | 0xFFFFFF00;
884: 		}
885: 
886: 		if ((cpu->temp2 & 0x80) == 0x80) {
887: 			cpu->temp2 = cpu->temp2 | 0xFFFFFF00;
888: 		}
889: 
890: 		cpu->temp3 = (cpu->temp1 * cpu->temp2) & 0xFFFF;
891: 		cpu->regs.wordregs[regax] = cpu->temp3 & 0xFFFF;
892: 		if (cpu->regs.byteregs[regah]) {
893: 			cpu->cf = 1;
894: 			cpu->of = 1;
895: 		}
896: 		else {
897: 			cpu->cf = 0;
898: 			cpu->of = 0;
899: 		}
900: #ifdef CPU_CLEAR_ZF_ON_MUL
901: 		cpu->zf = 0;
902: #endif
903: 		break;
904: 
905: 	case 6: /* DIV */
906: 		op_div8(cpu, cpu->regs.wordregs[regax], cpu->oper1b);
907: 		break;
908: 
909: 	case 7: /* IDIV */
910: 		op_idiv8(cpu, cpu->regs.wordregs[regax], cpu->oper1b);
911: 		break;
912: 	}
913: }

930: FUNC_INLINE void op_idiv16(CPU_t* cpu, uint32_t valdiv, uint16_t divisor) {

1029: 		cpu->zf = 0;

1031: 		break;
1032: 
1033: 	case 6: /* DIV */

1035: 		break;
1036: 
1037: 	case 7: /* DIV */
1038: 		op_idiv16(cpu, ((uint32_t)cpu->regs.wordregs[regdx] << 16) + cpu->regs.wordregs[regax], cpu->oper1);

1043: FUNC_INLINE void op_grp5(CPU_t* cpu) {
1044: 	switch (cpu->reg) {
1045: 	case 0: /* INC Ev */
1046: 		cpu->oper2 = 1;
1047: 		cpu->tempcf = cpu->cf;
1048: 		op_add16(cpu);
1049: 		cpu->cf = cpu->tempcf;
1050: 		writerm16(cpu, cpu->rm, cpu->res16);
1051: 		break;
1052: 
1053: 	case 1: /* DEC Ev */
1054: 		cpu->oper2 = 1;
1055: 		cpu->tempcf = cpu->cf;
1056: 		op_sub16(cpu);
1057: 		cpu->cf = cpu->tempcf;
1058: 		writerm16(cpu, cpu->rm, cpu->res16);
1059: 		break;
1060: 
1061: 	case 2: /* CALL Ev */
1062: 		push(cpu, cpu->ip);
1063: 		cpu->ip = cpu->oper1;
1064: 		break;
1065: 
1066: 	case 3: /* CALL Mp */
1067: 		push(cpu, cpu->segregs[regcs]);
1068: 		push(cpu, cpu->ip);
1069: 		getea(cpu, cpu->rm);
1070: 		cpu->ip = (uint16_t)cpu_read(cpu, cpu->ea) + (uint16_t)cpu_read(cpu, cpu->ea + 1) * 256;
1071: 		cpu->segregs[regcs] = (uint16_t)cpu_read(cpu, cpu->ea + 2) + (uint16_t)cpu_read(cpu, cpu->ea + 3) * 256;
1072: 		break;
1073: 
1074: 	case 4: /* JMP Ev */
1075: 		cpu->ip = cpu->oper1;
1076: 		break;
1077: 
1078: 	case 5: /* JMP Mp */
1079: 		getea(cpu, cpu->rm);
1080: 		cpu->ip = (uint16_t)cpu_read(cpu, cpu->ea) + (uint16_t)cpu_read(cpu, cpu->ea + 1) * 256;
1081: 		cpu->segregs[regcs] = (uint16_t)cpu_read(cpu, cpu->ea + 2) + (uint16_t)cpu_read(cpu, cpu->ea + 3) * 256;
1082: 		break;
1083: 
1084: 	case 6: /* PUSH Ev */
1085: 		push(cpu, cpu->oper1);
1086: 		break;
1087: 	}
1088: }

1090: FUNC_INLINE void cpu_intcall(CPU_t* cpu, uint8_t intnum) {
1091: 	if (cpu->int_callback[intnum] != NULL) {
1092: 		(*cpu->int_callback[intnum])(cpu, intnum);
1093: 		return;
1094: 	}
1095: 
1096: 	push(cpu, makeflagsword(cpu));
1097: 	push(cpu, cpu->segregs[regcs]);
1098: 	push(cpu, cpu->ip);
1099: 	cpu->segregs[regcs] = getmem16(cpu, 0, (uint16_t)intnum * 4 + 2);
1100: 	cpu->ip = getmem16(cpu, 0, (uint16_t)intnum * 4);
1101: 	cpu->ifl = 0;
1102: 	cpu->tf = 0;
1103: }

1105: void cpu_interruptCheck(CPU_t* cpu, I8259_t* i8259) {
1106: 	/* get next interrupt from the i8259, if any */
1107: 	if (!cpu->trap_toggle && (cpu->ifl && (i8259->irr & (~i8259->imr)))) {
1108: 		cpu->hltstate = 0;
1109: 		cpu_intcall(cpu, i8259_nextintr(i8259));
1110: 	}
1111: }

1113: void cpu_exec(CPU_t* cpu, uint32_t execloops) {
1114: 
1115: 	uint32_t loopcount;
1116: 	uint8_t docontinue;
1117: 	static uint16_t firstip;
1118: 
1119: 	for (loopcount = 0; loopcount < execloops; loopcount++) {
1120: 
1121: 		if (cpu->trap_toggle) {
1122: 			cpu_intcall(cpu, 1);
1123: 		}
1124: 
1125: 		if (cpu->tf) {
1126: 			cpu->trap_toggle = 1;
1127: 		}
1128: 		else {
1129: 			cpu->trap_toggle = 0;
1130: 		}
1131: 
1132: 		if (cpu->hltstate) goto skipexecution;
1133: 
1134: 		cpu->reptype = 0;

1154: 
1155: 			case 0x3E:	/* segment cpu->segregs[regds] */

1157: 				cpu->segoverride = 1;

1160: 			case 0x26:	/* segment cpu->segregs[reges] */

1175: 			case 0xF2:	/* REPNE/REPNZ */

1179: 			default:

1181: 				break;
1182: 			}
1183: 		}

1185: 		cpu->totalexec++;
1186: 
1187: 		switch (cpu->opcode) {

1196: 		case 0x1:	/* 01 ADD Ev Gv */

36: uint8_t i8255_readport(I8255_t* i8255, uint16_t portnum) {
37: #ifdef DEBUG_PPI
38: 	debug_log(DEBUG_DETAIL, "[I8255] Read port %02X\r\n", portnum);
39: #endif
40: 	portnum &= 7;
41: 	switch (portnum) {
42: 	case 0:
43: 		return i8255->keystate->scancode;
44: 	case 1:
45: 		return i8255->portB;
46: 	case 2:
47: 		//debug_log(DEBUG_DETAIL, "read 0x62\r\n");
48: 		if (i8255->portB & 8) {
49: 			return i8255->sw2 >> 4;
50: 		} else {
51: 			return i8255->sw2 & 0x0F;
52: 		}
53: 	}
54: 	return 0xFF;
55: }

57: void i8255_writeport(I8255_t* i8255, uint16_t portnum, uint8_t value) {
58: #ifdef DEBUG_PPI
59: 	debug_log(DEBUG_DETAIL, "[I8255] Write port %02X <- %02X\r\n", portnum, value);
60: #endif
61: 	portnum &= 7;
62: 	switch (portnum) {
63: 	case 0:
64: 		i8255->keystate->scancode = 0xAA;
65: 		break;
66: 	case 1:
67: 		if (value & 0x01) {
68: 			pcspeaker_selectGate(i8255->pcspeaker, PC_SPEAKER_USE_TIMER2);
69: #ifdef DEBUG_PPI
70: 			debug_log(DEBUG_DETAIL, "[I8255] Speaker take input from timer 2\r\n");
71: #endif
72: 		} else {
73: 			pcspeaker_selectGate(i8255->pcspeaker, PC_SPEAKER_USE_DIRECT);
74: #ifdef DEBUG_PPI
75: 			debug_log(DEBUG_DETAIL, "[I8255] Speaker take input from direct\r\n");
76: #endif
77: 		}
78: 		pcspeaker_setGateState(i8255->pcspeaker, PC_SPEAKER_GATE_DIRECT, (value >> 1) & 1);
79: #ifdef DEBUG_PPI
80: 		debug_log(DEBUG_DETAIL, "[I8255] Speaker direct value = %u\r\n", (value >> 1) & 1);
81: #endif

84: #ifdef DEBUG_PPI
85: 			debug_log(DEBUG_DETAIL, "[I8255] Keyboard reset\r\n");
86: #endif
87: 		}

89: 		break;
90: 	}
91: }

        if (cpu->trap_toggle) {
            cpu_intcall(cpu, 1);
        }
        if (cpu->tf) {
            cpu->trap_toggle = 1;
        } else {
            cpu->trap_toggle = 0;
        }
        if (cpu->hltstate) goto skipexecution;
        cpu->reptype = 0;
        cpu->segoverride = 0;
        cpu->useseg = cpu->segregs[regds];
        docontinue = 0;
        firstip = cpu->ip;
        while (!docontinue) {
            cpu->segregs[regcs] = cpu->segregs[regcs] & 0xFFFF;
            cpu->ip = cpu->ip & 0xFFFF;
            cpu->savecs = cpu->segregs[regcs];
            cpu->saveip = cpu->ip;
            cpu->opcode = getmem8(cpu, cpu->segregs[regcs], cpu->ip);
            StepIP(cpu, 1);
            switch (cpu->opcode) {
                case 0x2E: cpu->useseg = cpu->segregs[regcs]; cpu->segoverride = 1; break;
                case 0x3E: cpu->useseg = cpu->segregs[regds]; cpu->segoverride = 1; break;
                case 0x26: cpu->useseg = cpu->segregs[reges]; cpu->segoverride = 1; break;
                case 0x36: cpu->useseg = cpu->segregs[regss]; cpu->segoverride = 1; break;
                case 0xF3: cpu->reptype = 1; break;
                case 0xF2: cpu->reptype = 2; break;
                default: docontinue = 1; break;
            }
        }
        cpu->totalexec++;
        switch (cpu->opcode) {
            ...
        }
    }
}

This looks correct. The CPU reads opcodes in a loop, handling prefixes.

But wait, there's an issue. The `getmem8` macro is:
```c
#define getmem8(mycpu, x, y)	cpu_read(mycpu, segbase(x) + y)
```

And `segbase` is:
```c
#define segbase(x)	((uint32_t) x << 4)
```

So `getmem8(cpu, cpu->segregs[regcs], cpu->ip)` = `cpu_read(cpu, (cpu->segregs[regcs] << 4) + cpu->ip)`.

This computes the physical address as (CS << 4) + IP.

If CS = 0xF000, IP = 0xE85B:
physical = (0xF000 << 4) + 0xE85B = 0xF0000 + 0xE85B = 0xFE85B.
